patients.label: 50-year-old man with infectious arthritis of the left knee who developed severe hemolytic anemia after knee replacement and died

identity_evidence.quote: we report a case of a 50-year-old man

attribution_limitations: The text prints the third antibody screening cell as III(±) while Table 1 prints w (weakly positive per its footnote); both notations denote a weak reaction, so this is treated as a notation difference, not a value conflict.
Source conflict on vancomycin frequency: the abstract says intravenously every day postoperatively, the case text says 1 g every 12 h; the source does not reconcile them.

The case text says an emergency blood transfusion was required on the eighth postoperative day and separately that three units of RBCs were received that evening; it does not state they are the same event.
The authors judge the fatal cerebral infarction and subsequent shock highly likely to be direct consequences of the severe hemolytic anemia.
The authors state no cause of the prior cerebral infarction was found in hospital records and argue early-onset ischemic stroke was highly likely from the comorbidities.
Anti-N is described as suspected, possible and likely, and as likely an autoantibody; the final conclusion is vancomycin-dependent antibodies specific for the N antigen.
The authors say the patient had repeated exposure to vancomycin and had received a large amount; number, dates and doses of exposures other than the stated regimen are not given.
The authors acknowledge potential hemolytic effects of other concomitant medications were not systematically excluded by antibody testing.
The authors suggest residual drug in the serum probably explains positive screening results and that an IgM-to-IgG transition may have occurred; these are hypotheses.
The abstract reports presence of hemoglobin in urine and the case text reports positive urinary occult blood; the source does not state these are the same test or result.
Only the Table 1 footnote defines the 0 grade (no agglutination); Tables 2 and 3 print 0 cells without their own legend.

evidence.quote: Patient’s hemoglobin and indirect bilirubin levels after hospital admission.

limitations: Figure 1 values and annotations are pixel content recorded in the visual submission only; the hemoglobin 44 g/L and indirect bilirubin 131.4 μmol/L values also appear in the text and are recorded from it.
Reagent-cell antigen profiles in Tables 1 to 3 are reagent properties, not patient results, and are not recorded as patient facts.
Several discussion statements are author hypotheses (residual drug, IgM to IgG transition, causal link to cerebral infarction) and are kept as ambiguities.
Hospital admission is dated December 2024 in the case text; no exact dates are given for the surgery, transfusion or death beyond postoperative days.
No supplementary material is listed for this article.
Table 1 defines 0 as no agglutination; Tables 2 and 3 print 0 without their own legend, so their zero cells are flagged negative only where the text states no agglutination or no reactivity.
Table 3 rows using normal AB-type serum are laboratory control experiments with another person’s serum and are not recorded as patient results.
Vancomycin frequency conflicts between the abstract (every day) and the case text (every 12 h); only the frequency is quarantined as review-only.
